deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivations, formulas or computations. It is a set of methodological and philosophical notes, consistent with the surrounding pages of the notebook: equality as a relative concept and 'Mathematik ist die Kunst des Nichtrechnens' on p.103, and Kronecker's dictum and the axioms of physics vs. geometry on p.105.

Content, paragraph by paragraph:

(1) Fragment of a contrast between mathematician and physicist. The mathematician needs only Vorstellungen (mental representations) and 'experiments, as it were, even without the help of the senses'. The physicist still works mainly through the senses, i.e. directly with sensory impressions.

This opening sentence is grammatically incomplete. It almost certainly continues the last line of the page numbered 105: 'Zwischen dem Mathematiker und Physiker ... besteht allerdings doch der Unterschied, dass der Mathematiker als Objekt für das Ordnen, d.h. für seine Untersuchung bloss | Vorstellungen braucht ...'. So folio [104] logically follows [105] in the writing sequence. Either the leaves are out of order, or Hilbert wrote across facing pages in a non-linear way. Previous page 103 ends with a complete sentence, which supports this reading.

(2) The sources of mathematics' power do not lie in its applications to physics, astronomy, etc. This is an anti-utilitarian, internalist claim about the strength of mathematics.

(3) Historical periodization. The development of mathematics is divided into three periods: naive, formal and critical. 'We' (Hilbert's generation) have arrived in the critical period.
- Criticism alone would be sterile.
- It must therefore not merely purify the large stock of material inherited from the formal period by eliminating things.
- It must also connect that material: by holding different viewpoints together, by taking manifold routes, and by fitting together seemingly heterogeneous objects.
- This is where the true fruitfulness and the future of the critical period lie.
- Klein seeks this unifying element in geometry; Hilbert ('ich') seeks it in analysis.

Nothing implicit needs to be filled in mathematically.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is philosophical and contains no new mathematics. The naive/formal/critical periodization and similar aphorisms from Hilbert's notebooks are known to historians. The explicit, almost programmatic statement that Klein seeks unification in geometry and Hilbert in analysis is a nice self-characterization. It is mildly notable given that Hilbert later produced the Grundlagen der Geometrie, but it is not a major finding.
